misconception.description: dividing the cushion by break-even sales instead of by budgeted sales, which compares the headroom with the wrong base and overstates it

worked_example.text: A ski school budgets revenue of EUR 500,000 for the season and works out that it covers all its costs at EUR 350,000 of revenue.
worked_example.solution: The cushion is 500,000 - 350,000 = EUR 150,000. Against budgeted revenue that is 150,000 / 500,000 = 0.3, a margin of safety of 30%.

problem.text: A hotel budgets revenue of EUR 1,000,000 for next year and calculates that it breaks even at EUR 800,000 of revenue. What is its margin of safety as a percentage of budgeted revenue?

distractors.note: the documented misconception: the cushion divided by break-even revenue
reporting the share of the plan that must be achieved rather than the cushion above it

hints: Start with the distance in euros between what the hotel plans to take and what it must take to cover its costs. That distance is the cushion.
A percentage is always a percentage of something. Here the question names budgeted revenue, so that is what goes underneath the fraction.
Divide the euro cushion by budgeted revenue and read the result as a percentage of the plan.
worked_solution: Step 1: the cushion is 1,000,000 - 800,000 = EUR 200,000 of revenue that could be lost before the hotel stops covering its costs. Step 2: divide by the base the question names, budgeted revenue: 200,000 / 1,000,000 = 0.2, a margin of safety of 20%. One booking season in five could disappear before trouble starts. Dividing by break-even revenue instead would report 25%, which sounds safer and answers a different question: it compares the cushion with the revenue the hotel must make, not with the revenue it plans to make.

near_transfer.text: The same hotel budgets EUR 1,000,000 of revenue, breaks even at EUR 800,000, and sells room-nights at an average of EUR 200. What is its margin of safety measured in room-nights?

distractors.note: reporting the whole budgeted volume instead of the cushion
reporting the break-even volume instead of the cushion

far_transfer.text: A restaurant reports a margin of safety of 25% and breaks even at EUR 600,000 of revenue. What revenue has it budgeted?

distractors.note: adding the margin to break-even revenue, which uses break-even as the base
dividing by the margin instead of by one minus the margin
